page: Amazon Web Services c8g.large is a compute-optimized arm64 instance driven by AWS Graviton processors built on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz. Provisioned on the AWS Nitro System, the instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with one thread per core. Memory capacity is configured at 4.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptographic acceleration. The instance does not bundle local NVMe storage and contains zero GPUs, routing storage I/O externally while maintaining a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks reflect consistent single-thread responsiveness alongside lower aggregate throughput dictated by the 2-core configuration. Single-core tests show 1706.89 in stress-ng and 1763.0 in Geekbench, placing the processor in the middle 50% tier of cloud instances. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression performs well at 14.15 GB/sec. Conversely, total parallel throughput benchmarks register in lower brackets, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 3170.0 and a multi-threaded stress-ng score of 3402.99. Memory benchmarks show uncached 256MB block read throughput of 55.26 GB/sec and write throughput of 22.16 GB/sec. In application-level benchmarks, Redis SET operations record 4.5 million operations per second, and static web serving delivers 4.89 GB/sec throughput.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the c8g.large provides dedicated physical execution threads at a low resource footprint, eliminating hyperthread contention without requiring a large instance size. The primary operational tradeoff is the absence of ephemeral instance storage and modest memory capacity, requiring external volume attachments for persistent data. This instance profile is appropriate for microservices, lightweight API backends, containerized web applications, entry-level CI/CD build nodes, and decoupled background worker queues.
description: Amazon Web Services c8g.large is a compute-optimized arm64 instance driven by an AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. Virtualized via the Nitro System, it provides 2 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, paired with 4.0 GB of RAM. The instance features a 36 MB L3 cache and hardware AES encryption. It does not include local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate balanced single-core execution, producing a 1763.0 single-core Geekbench score and 14.15 GB/sec bzip3 decompression throughput, though multi-core performance remains limited by the two-core boundary. The c8g.large offers resource-dense dedicated compute suited for lightweight microservices, front-end web serving, API endpoints, and low-scale queue processing tasks.
